sourceEvidence.claim: Chronic inflammation — the definition: prolonged, mononuclear infiltration (macrophages, lymphocytes, plasma cells), simultaneous tissue destruction and repair (angiogenesis and fibrosis); may be preceded by acute inflammation
sourceEvidence.quote:
Prolonged inflammation characterized by mononuclear infiltration (macrophages, lymphocytes,
plasma cells), which leads to simultaneous tissue destruction and repair (including angiogenesis
and fibrosis). May be preceded by acute inflammation.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Chronic STIMULI — persistent infections (TB, T pallidum, certain fungi and viruses) → type IV hypersensitivity; autoimmune; toxic agents (silica); foreign material
sourceEvidence.quote:
STIMULI

Persistent infections (eg, TB, T pallidum, certain fungi and viruses) → type IV hypersensitivity,
autoimmune diseases, prolonged exposure to toxic agents (eg, silica) and foreign material.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Chronic MEDIATORS — macrophages dominant; the Th1 → IFN-γ → classical activation (proinflammatory) and Th2 → IL-4/IL-13 → alternative activation (repair, anti-inflammatory) fork
sourceEvidence.quote:
MeDIATORS

Macrophages are the dominant cells. Interaction of macrophages and T cells → chronic
inflammation.
▘ Th1 cells secrete IFN-γ → macrophage classical activation (proinflammatory)
▘ Th2 cells secrete IL-4 and IL-13 → macrophage alternative activation (repair and antiinflammatory)
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Chronic OUTCOMES — scarring, amyloidosis, neoplastic transformation; the HCV → hepatocellular carcinoma and H pylori → chronic gastritis → gastric adenocarcinoma chains
sourceEvidence.quote:
OUTCOMeS

Scarring, amyloidosis, and neoplastic transformation (eg, chronic HCV infection → chronic
inflammation → hepatocellular carcinoma; Helicobacter pylori infection → chronic gastritis
→ gastric adenocarcinoma).
